string-array.item: Justnoise Android internal beta — Privacy Policy draft

Draft updated: 2026-09-07. This text is for the planned local-only com.justnoise.app beta with local History and the connected native schedule flow, not a claim that device or release acceptance has finished. It does not describe the iOS app, web shop, or Android/Google Play\'s own services. Validate it against the release package before publication.

Draft — not yet published. The owner supplied the publisher and contact below on 2026-09-07. The public Android privacy-policy URL is still a placeholder, and final release review remains pending. Business-registration details and email delivery have not been independently verified.
App/brand: Justnoise
Publisher: Justnoise Media
Privacy contact: hello@justnoise.shop
Public privacy-policy URL: [YOUR PUBLISHED ANDROID PRIVACY POLICY URL]
For questions about this policy or your local app data, contact the publisher using the privacy contact above.

Justnoise helps you interrupt apps you select during a focus session. This candidate has no app accounts, purchases, cloud sync, advertising, analytics or crash-reporting service. It does not transmit the data below to us or third parties or sell them.

While you have enabled its Accessibility service, Justnoise receives window-change event types and foreground app identifiers, including when no focus session is active. Only the latest identifier is held temporarily in service memory to re-evaluate an already-open target at scheduled start; it is cleared on screen off, service interruption/disconnection and uncertain locked/noninteractive refresh. There is no identifier sequence, disk retention or event log. The interruption is shown only for an app in the active session\'s saved target snapshot during an eligible active session. It does not read screen contents, typed text, passwords, notifications or accessibility nodes, or save a foreground-app history.

A temporary generation counter and main-thread readiness acknowledgment check the same bound service/foreground state during scheduled-start preflight. This is not an atomic guarantee of OS readiness through later disk I/O; uncertain state after start follows the existing interruption/recovery path. The acknowledgment waits at most 750 ms; its readiness lease lasts at most one second and becomes invalid after a relevant state change, disconnect or expiry. These in-memory values are not saved, logged or used as telemetry.

You can keep up to 30 named modes locally. Each stores a stable ID, revision, a trimmed name of up to 60 characters and up to 500 chosen app identifiers. The app also stores the last mode you explicitly selected for manual Zap starts. Saving or running a scheduled mode does not change that selection. Missing or empty modes cannot start and are never replaced by another mode. An existing saved selection migrates to Noise with the stable local-default ID; no old selection means an empty catalog. Deleting all modes does not recreate defaults. Mode edits, deletion and selection are blocked during a requested session or recovery. Any referencing schedule, including a disabled one, prevents mode deletion. Deleting the recent mode clears that selection without fallback. These data remain until edited or deleted, withdrawal, app-data clear or uninstall. Mode names and identifiers are not added to completed History or notification content.

The local app picker reads launchable app names and identifiers. Justnoise also reads system app identifiers, service-enablement metadata and screen/inset geometry for readiness and safe navigation. These observations are temporary. Session and pairing configuration includes your selected targets, active-mode ID/name, active-session identity/target snapshot/clocks/process identity, last-finished session ID, consent version/time, session state/revision, interruption/recovery and service-liveness state, and the keyed digest used to recognize your paired tag. The first-run introduction also saves a local completed/not-completed flag. Android temporarily retains its current page, route and a failed-save marker when recreating the screen. These values do not grant Accessibility consent or start a session, and the completed flag is removed with local withdrawal, app-data clear or uninstall. The silent introduction videos are bundled in the app. The optional Zap-store link opens an external website in your browser; that website has its own privacy terms. An originating schedule ID is also stored only while its scheduled session is active, for recovery when the foreground state is unknown. It is removed on successful stop, a manual start, withdrawal, app-data clear or uninstall, and is not included in completed History. NFC Text data is processed temporarily, not saved or logged; the tag\'s hardware identifier is read only in memory to check a registered Zap and is never saved, logged or sent. Configuration uses private app storage, and the digest\'s non-exportable key is managed by Android Keystore. Configuration is not claimed to be wholly encrypted. The app excludes its data from Android backup and transfer; this is not a guarantee about every manufacturer\'s restore behavior.

For History, Justnoise saves a random session ID, start and end times, non-negative duration, number of selected apps and whether continuity was interrupted. Completed History contains no app names or foreground-event log. It shows Session time, not verified continuously protected time; cross-process timing is marked interrupted. Stopping clears the active-mode ID/name, target snapshot and clocks and queues one local completed record for retryable insertion into a private SQLite database before a later start or History read. Stopping itself does not wait for database delivery. Repeated insertion of the same session ID must not add another record. History stays on this device until withdrawal, app-data clear or uninstall; there is no automatic expiry in this slice.

The schedule runtime stores up to 100 configurations in private app preferences: a random schedule ID, revision, name, enabled flag, one-time instant or repeating weekdays/local time, named creation time zone and the chosen mode ID. Existing references to local-default retain the migrated Noise mode. A schedule resolves its own mode\'s then-current apps at start, not the recent manual selection; missing or empty references cannot start and do not fall back to another mode. It also stores one pending occurrence, independent last-resolved local-date and one-time-instant markers, and only the latest outcome for each schedule. An occurrence contains schedule ID/revision, nominal key, fire time, local date where applicable and zone; an outcome adds a result code, handled time and session ID only if a start committed. Markers survive edits to prevent replay. Configuration and execution records remain until that schedule is deleted, consent withdrawal, app-data clear or uninstall. Completed scheduled sessions use the same History path and retention as manual sessions; deleting a schedule does not delete History. The native editor offers one-time date/time or repeating weekdays and uses the referenced mode\'s current app selection at each start. A retained ViewModel and Android-managed saved-instance-state Bundle may keep the route and unsaved editor fields, original revision and original one-time instant/zone for Activity/process recreation. This adds no separate app preference/database schema. Unsaved state is discarded on successful save, Cancel/explicit discard or observed consent revocation. If the process ends while a save may be in progress, restoration warns that its result is uncertain; the app does not automatically repeat the change. Explicit reload discards unsaved edits. A transient consent timestamp frozen for each mutation rejects queued changes after withdrawal, even if current consent is later accepted again.

The app temporarily checks its own process startup evidence: PID/name and Force Stop status on Android API 35+, or its own exit reason/time on API 31–34. It does not save or log those raw records or inspect other apps\' process history. A local suspension flag and foreground-recovery acknowledgment time prevent unattended recovery; the flag clears after successful acknowledgment and the timestamp remains until replaced, withdrawal, app-data clear or uninstall. Older Android exit evidence is conservative and can require recovery after other user-requested process exits.

Schedules use separately granted exact-alarm access, boot/system-change callbacks and a partial wake lock. A non-exported receiver revalidates local state with at most one running and one queued delivery; each has a 9-second wake-lock lease and an 8-second processing budget including queue wait. The alarm is replaced/canceled through Android; worker state is transient. A callback alone is not proof of a session start. Delivery can be delayed or missed, and stopped-state recovery does not catch up old starts. No new network destination or analytics is introduced. The separate alarm Settings button is offered only for requested-enabled schedules with missing access and opens Settings only when pressed. Saving alone does not grant access; enabled configuration can be retained while setup is still required.

Withdraw consent and clear Gate 0 data attempts to remove saved modes/recent selection, active-mode identity and other configuration, pending/completed History, schedule/execution/recovery state and the pairing key, cancel the alarm and disable the service. A durable cleanup marker retries an interrupted database deletion before new consent, session start or History access. Success and incomplete cleanup have different feedback; if cleanup cannot be confirmed, retry or use Android App info to clear storage or uninstall. Disabling Accessibility alone stops service access but does not erase saved configuration or History. There is no server account to delete. Raw foreground events and NFC payloads are not retained as History. Affirmative v4 disclosure consent is required for new starts/service use; earlier consent is not silently upgraded. Existing v3 active sessions keep their prior History eligibility; v1/v2 sessions are not backfilled. Verify the connected schedule editor/enable and separate exact-alarm permission flow before release; local checks and the bounded emulator UI smoke are not full UI, A16 or policy acceptance.

If you separately allow notifications, Justnoise can display generic session time or an attention message in Android\'s notification panel and, depending on your system settings, on the lock screen. It includes no mode names/IDs, selected-app names or tag data. Tapping opens the app; dismissing does not end the session. One matching session ID is saved locally to keep a dismissed display hidden for that session; it is removed with withdrawal, app-data clear or uninstall. Notification refusal does not prevent sessions. The display is not proof of uninterrupted blocking: if Android abruptly ends the process, its last display may remain until the next reconciliation. Known stops and withdrawal cancel it. There is no notification foreground service, tracking or network destination.

The detailed implementation inventory is DATA_INVENTORY.md (DATA_INVENTORY.md). Before publishing, confirm the supplied contact can receive messages, review the final release\'s actual data handling, host this notice at a public non-geofenced HTML URL, and expose the policy in the app and Play Console. The current separate Accessibility disclosure is not a substitute for a full privacy policy. These publication requirements follow Google\'s User Data policy (https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10144311). Apps exclusively on internal testing are exempt from the Data safety form, not the applicable privacy/disclosure duties; see Google\'s Data safety guidance (https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469).
